research_question: In a separate, balanced 2024 Terceira survey with ten original native and ten exotic-secondary forest plots, do endemic, native nonendemic and introduced arthropods show different absolute native-vs-exotic habitat preferences at the same SLAM vertical sampling opportunity, and is this direction consistent with the older, sealed SLAM 2012–2022 island-level source observation?

original_2024_source.field_design_original_paper: 20 separate 20m×20m Terceira plots; 10 native intact wet forest vs 10 secondary exotic-tree forest; 3 SLAM traps at different heights per plot and supplementary 14 Pitfall traps per plot. Reconcile original source Event identity/effort before species.
original_2024_source.published_prior_art: 2025 original FERM paper: vertical arthropod similarity decays with trap-height difference and vertical decay slopes did not significantly differ between native and exotic forests; non-indigenous taxa narrower vertical distributions. These original ecology findings are PRIOR ART, not independent Structural discoveries.

earlier_fixed_Azores_comparator.source: Azores 2012–2022 42 SLAM forest traps, 33 eligible plots in Flores/Pico/Terceira and 664 Event observations
earlier_fixed_Azores_comparator.comparator_limit: 2024 data arise in same Terceira island and potentially overlapping forest fragments/trap locations, so distinct survey year/source does NOT ensure independent ecological site-level or archipelago replication. Original 2024 capture format differs in vertical stratification and sample effort.

response_blind_sequence: v1.332 verify exact ZIP SHA and Darwin Core source Event/Occurrence field term roles from ORIGINAL meta.xml and central directory ONLY; open neither Event nor Occurrence biological bodies.

v1.333 original Event-only physical 20 site labels and author native/exotic habitat, sampling method SLAM vs Pitfall, source trap height/vertical stratum, date and equal method/height replicate count. Pre-frozen minimum 8 native and 8 exotic original plots, source same seasonal campaign, and at least one equal-effort SLAM trap height with one source Event per plot. Choose selected stratum based on source-only effort coverage, not taxa.

v1.334 freeze exact primary site-level identified endemic/non-endemic native/introduced richness for original SLAM trap stratum, analysis unit 20 physical forest plots; original event-to-occurrence join, origin ontology and ability to detect at least 8 sites per side with taxa before first Occurrence source read. Compare source-native and source-exotic absolute richness, separate status and a double-contrast, no plot/trap pseudo-independent p-values.

If original source Event site/height/habitat fields insufficient, STOP the strict 2024 forest-origin replication rather than pooling pitfall with SLAM or guessing trap height from taxon data. Nothing reopened from previous Azores SLAM, BALA or PRIBES sources.
scientific_ceiling: Original 2024 data used by published 2025 vertical-decay article; current interpretation cannot claim published origin vertical range finding as a new result.
Single Terceira island, not new archipelago. Plot/fragment overlap with older SLAM not verified. Independence limited to public field source and collection year.
Site habitat native versus secondary exotic not randomized. Source sampling height, trap/effort, forest altitude and landscape conditions may confound richness differences.
A site-level richness gradient is not demographic persistence, post-introduction survival, biotic interactions, invasions into forests or island migration.
Original 2024 occurrence file includes only named taxa; unknown taxon proportion might differ by forest habitat. Report source taxonomic coverage.
No original BALA/SLAM2012-22/PRIBES biological replay, no eBird.
